thread:
Mira Chen: quick heads-up — we started seeing a 20-40% P99 tail latency regression when speculative decoding pairs qwen-14 (primary) with mixtral-8 (draft) under bursty traffic. noticed ~22:14 UTC yesterday and it stays until drafts stop. infra-bot: alert #4231 triggered at 22:15 :rotating_light:
Oliver Park: timeline + any recent runtime changes?
Mira Chen: we rolled a kernel-selection tweak in canary that prefers fused_matmul for small batches (<8) to speed qwen kernels. looked fine on microbenchmarks but prod traces show lots of extra memcpy and kvcache misses on the draft path.
Cheng Li: interesting — could be kvcache shape mismatch when we stitch cache entries from different family (qwen qkv dim vs mixtral). did we change padding/kv-layout?
Mira Chen: not intentionally. profiler shows repeated cache invalidations at sequence boundary: 
```
kvcache.hits: 62% -> 18% with pairing
kvcache.evictions: up 3x
kernel_switches: frequent (fused_matmul <-> cutlass)
latency_per_token: +12ms median
```
Dana R.: also saw tokenization drift in a few sampled requests — some multi-byte tokens were split differently between the two tokenizers, which increases step count and invalidates prefix cache.
Oliver Park: tokenizer mismatch + kv-layout mismatch = double whammy. We should treat draft pairing as family-aware.
Cheng Li: agree. immediate mitigations: (1) pin draft models to same tokenizer family or run normalization step, (2) force unified kv-layout / canonical padding for paired requests, (3) fall back to pure-cpu draft if kv-layout incompatible.
Mira Chen: short-term config I pushed to canary: 
```
model_pairing:
  allow_mixed_tokenizers: false
  kv_layout: canonical_fullpad
  kernel_priority: ["fused_matmul","cutlass","cublas"]
  speculative_accept_threshold: 0.28
```
Mira Chen: lowering speculative_accept_threshold dropped speculative completions by ~35% in canary, which reduced draft traffic and P99 by ~18%. but that also raised average cost slightly.
Oliver Park: can we instead adjust batching heuristics? e.g., increase batching window for paired requests to 6ms to improve kernel utilization and reduce frequent kernel switches.
Cheng Li: increasing batching helped on qwen-only, but for mixed-family it delays the moment we realize tokenization divergence and increases wasted prefixes. maybe conditional: if pairing detected, use conservative batching (shorter window) + canonicalization.
Dana R.: on RoPE scaling: pairings where models had different RoPE scaling (mixtral small-scale vs qwen standard) caused attention misalignment when we tried to reuse KV slices. We should add a RoPE compatibility check to the pairing planner.
Mira Chen: agreed — action: add pair_compatibility check that validates {vocab_family, kv_dim, head_count, rope_scale}. fail open? fail closed?
Oliver Park: prefer fail-closed for production (reject pairing) and log suggestion to fallback to model-variant with compatible dims. For lower tiers we can allow pairing with on-the-fly remap but with higher SLO guardrails.
qa-bot: perf-regression-ticket created: RFC-PR-981 with profiling artifacts and flamegraphs.
Cheng Li: long-term idea: implement a lightweight pairing oracle that records per-model kernel profiles + tokenizer fingerprint. When pairing, simulate expected token-growth and KV footprint and reject if mispredicted. That avoids expensive runtime evictions.
Mira Chen: next steps I propose:
- Mira: roll config to prod w/ allow_mixed_tokenizers=false and kv_layout canonical for pairing (in next 15m)
- Oliver: test conditional batching tweak in staging (increase window for matched-families, keep short for mixed)
- Cheng: add RoPE/kv_dim compatibility check to planner (PR by EOD)
- Dana: run tokenization sweep across top 50 prompts to build mapping table (tomorrow)
- infra-bot: keep alerting on kvcache.evictions and speculative_accept_rate drop
Oliver Park: quick command to reproduce locally: 
```
python infra/profiler/run.py --pair qwen-14:mixtral-8 --samples 2000 --trace kernels,kvcache,tokenizer
```
Mira Chen: thanks — we will monitor. if anyone sees oddities ping me directly. :thumbsup:
